annotations.description: Discarded Commune with Lava, which is an excellent instant that synergizes powerfully with Kalamax (gets copied when Kalamax is tapped, doubling the card advantage). Kept Swarm Intelligence (7 mana) instead, which won't be castable for many turns. Commune with Lava is flexible and scales well at any point in the game.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Frantic Search (reasonable), but discarded Commune with Lava and Forest, keeping Swarm Intelligence (7 mana), Melek (6 mana), Rashmi (4 mana), and Twinning Staff.
annotations.betterLine: Should have discarded Swarm Intelligence instead of Commune with Lava. Swarm Intelligence costs 7 mana and is the least likely to be cast soon, while Commune with Lava is a key synergy piece with the Kalamax commander that provides scalable card advantage at instant speed.

annotations.description: The player cast Master of the Pearl Trident before playing their Forest from hand. They have a Forest in hand and only 2 lands on the battlefield (Simic Growth Chamber + Island). By playing the Forest first, they would have 3 lands available. While they can cast Master of the Pearl Trident with UU from their current lands, playing the land first is generally better sequencing - it represents more mana available on future turns sooner, and there's no reason to delay the land drop. The Forest should have been played before casting the spell.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Master of the Pearl Trident (UU) without first playing Forest from hand.
annotations.betterLine: Play Forest first (making the land drop), then cast Master of the Pearl Trident. This ensures the land drop isn't missed and maximizes available mana going forward.

annotations.description: The player should play their Island from hand before casting Merfolk Sovereign. Playing the land first would give them access to 4 mana (Simic Growth Chamber + Island + Island + Forest) instead of 3, and with Tatyova in hand at 5 mana, getting the land drop in early is important. More critically, playing the land before casting the creature is almost always correct sequencing - there's no reason to hold the land. Additionally, casting a creature before combat means the opponent sees the board state before blocks matter. While Master of the Pearl Trident is already on board and could attack, playing Merfolk Sovereign pre-combat telegraphs the +1/+1 buff.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Merfolk Sovereign without first playing the Island from hand.
annotations.betterLine: Play Island first (getting closer to casting Tatyova next turn with 5 lands), then cast Merfolk Sovereign. The land drop costs nothing and ensures no missed land drops.

annotations.description: Tatyova, Benthic Druid is a significantly stronger play here as a card advantage engine. Every subsequent land drop would draw a card and gain 1 life, which compounds over the game. Tributary Instructor is a decent body (6/6 with lords) but its abilities (mentor, draw on +1/+1 counter creature death) aren't immediately impactful and require setup. Tatyova would become a 5/5 with the lords while generating cards every turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Tributary Instructor (4/4 body, 6/6 with lords)
annotations.betterLine: Cast Tatyova, Benthic Druid for the same mana cost (GGUUU covers 3GU), getting a repeatable card draw engine that generates value on every land drop for the rest of the game.

annotations.description: With 5 mana available (Plains, Mountain, Swamp, Rootbound Crag + 1 more land), GPT5n Memoir passed the turn without casting any spells. They could have cast Tymna the Weaver (1WB, 3 mana) as a lifelink creature and card draw engine, plus a 2-mana creature like Zhur-Taa Druid or Sylvok Explorer, developing their board significantly on turn 6.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Rootbound Crag and passed the turn without casting any creatures.
annotations.betterLine: Play Rootbound Crag, then cast Tymna the Weaver (1WB) and Zhur-Taa Druid (RG) or Sylvok Explorer (1G) to develop the board and set up card draw for future turns.

annotations.description: Casting Kindred Discovery (5 mana) before combat means the player misses drawing cards from the 'attacks' trigger this turn, since the enchantment won't be on the battlefield during the declare attackers step if cast in precombat main... actually wait, precombat main IS before combat, so if they cast it now, it will be on the battlefield when they attack. However, they're spending all 5 mana on this enchantment, which means they can't cast Tatyova (also 5 mana) this turn. The real question is whether Tatyova, Benthic Druid would have been a better play - Tatyova draws cards on land drops and gains life, but Kindred Discovery with 3 Merfolk on board (Master of the Pearl Trident, Merfolk Sovereign, Tributary Instructor) will draw 3 cards on attack this turn. That's a strong immediate payoff. However, casting a 5-mana enchantment before combat telegraphs the attack plan and gives opponents information. More importantly, the player should consider whether Tatyova would be better since it's a body that can block/attack AND draws cards. But 3 immediate draws from attacks is very strong. This seems reasonable overall, though Tatyova as a Merfolk itself would also trigger Kindred Discovery later if sequenced differently. The play is defensible.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Kindred Discovery naming Merfolk in precombat main
annotations.betterLine: This is actually reasonable - Kindred Discovery before combat draws 3 cards from attacking Merfolk. Tatyova could also be considered but draws fewer cards immediately. The main concern is that casting before combat rather than holding up Curse of the Swine mana leaves no interaction, but with only 5 mana total this is a minor consideration.

annotations.description: Opus Minimal cast Tishana (7 mana: 5GU) before playing the Island from hand. Playing Island first would have meant one more card drawn from Tishana's ETB (since Tishana draws equal to creatures you control, not cards in hand - but more importantly, casting spells before playing lands is generally a sequencing error). Additionally, Stonybrook Banneret should have been cast first - it costs only 1U, and having it on the battlefield means one more creature when Tishana enters, drawing an additional card from Tishana's ETB trigger (5 creatures instead of 4). The correct sequence would be: play Island, cast Stonybrook Banneret (1U), then cast Tishana (5GU) with 5 creatures on board to draw 5 cards instead of 4.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Tishana directly with 4 creatures on board, drawing 4 cards.
annotations.betterLine: Play Island first, cast Stonybrook Banneret (1U) to have 5 creatures on board, then cast Tishana (5GU) to draw 5 cards instead of 4.

annotations.description: Haiku Optim is at 5 life with no flying blockers and mostly tapped lands. Chrome Courier (1/1 flying) + Indomitable Archangel (4/4 flying) = exactly 5 damage, which is lethal. Attacking with only Chrome Courier misses the kill.
annotations.actionTaken: Selected only Chrome Courier as attacker instead of all creatures
annotations.betterLine: Attack with both Chrome Courier and Indomitable Archangel directed at Haiku Optim for exactly lethal damage (5 flying damage vs 5 life)

annotations.description: Deeproot Elite trigger targets a Merfolk you control on the battlefield. The reasoning suggests pumping Tishana (which is in hand, not on the battlefield). Among battlefield Merfolk, Tributary Instructor has no +1/+1 counter yet, making it the best target - giving it a counter enables Inspiring Call to draw from it and trigger its death-draw ability, plus makes it a bigger mentor source.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose Tishana, Voice of Thunder (likely in hand, not on battlefield) reasoning to 'pump Tishana to 20/20'
annotations.betterLine: Put the +1/+1 counter on Tributary Instructor to enable its death-draw trigger and increase Inspiring Call value, or on another battlefield Merfolk without counters for maximum utility.
